1.title: Storage
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Storage. This module covers task statement three point six, identifying the A W S storage services. You will learn the three kinds of storage, object, block and file, how the Amazon S three storage classes differ, and how A W S helps you back up, archive and recover data. Storage questions are common on the exam, and most of them ask you to match a need to a service.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Tell object, block and file storage apart, and match each to an A W S service. Choose the right Amazon S three storage class, from Standard to Glacier Deep Archive. Explain S three Lifecycle rules and S three Versioning. Compare Amazon E B S and instance store, and Amazon E F S and Amazon F S x. And place A W S Storage Gateway, A W S Backup and A W S Elastic Disaster Recovery.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater's Data Grows
1.text: Tidewater's data is growing. Customers upload millions of product photos, which few people view after the sale. Order records must be kept for years, at the lowest cost. The shop's database server needs a fast disk, and the Linux web servers must share one set of files. The warehouse office keeps files on site, but wants cloud storage behind them. And the founder wants consistent backups, and a quick recovery if a server room is lost. Your job is to choose the right storage for each need.

1.title: Object, Block and File Storage
1.text: Start with the three kinds of storage. Object storage keeps objects, a file plus its metadata, in buckets. That is Amazon S three. Block storage gives a virtual disk to a server. That is Amazon E B S and instance store. File storage gives a shared file system that many servers can mount. That is Amazon E F S and Amazon F S x. On top of these sit archive and backup services: the S three Glacier classes, A W S Backup, and Elastic Disaster Recovery. And for access from your own data center, there is A W S Storage Gateway. Exam tip: name the type first. Is it objects, a disk for one server, or a shared file system?

1.title: Amazon S3: Object Storage at Any Scale
1.text: Amazon Simple Storage Service, or S three, is object storage. You store any amount of data as objects in buckets. Typical uses include websites, backup and restore, archives, data lakes and mobile apps. An object is a file plus metadata, and you find it by its key, which is its name inside the bucket. You choose the Region for each bucket, and objects never leave that Region unless you move or replicate them. Buckets and objects are private by default, and Block Public Access is on by default. You pay only for what you use, with no overage charges, and reads after writes are strongly consistent. Exam tip: unlimited, durable, internet-scale storage for files and media means Amazon S three.

1.title: S3 Storage Classes: Frequent and Infrequent Access
1.text: S three offers storage classes for different access patterns. S three Standard is the default, for frequently accessed data with millisecond access, in three or more Availability Zones. S three Intelligent-Tiering is for unknown or changing access patterns. It moves objects between tiers automatically, with no retrieval fees. S three Standard-I A is for long-lived, infrequently accessed data that still needs millisecond access. It has a thirty-day minimum and a retrieval fee. S three One Zone-I A is for re-creatable, infrequently accessed data. It uses one Availability Zone, so the data is lost if that zone is lost. S three Express One Zone, beyond the guide, gives single-digit millisecond access in one zone you choose. Every class listed is designed for eleven nines of durability. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, these figures come from the S three user guide. Exam tip: unknown pattern means Intelligent-Tiering, and re-creatable and cheaper means One Zone-I A.

1.title: S3 Glacier Classes: Archive Storage
1.text: For archives there are three Glacier classes. S three Glacier Instant Retrieval is for rarely accessed archives, read about once a quarter, but with millisecond access. It has a ninety-day minimum. S three Glacier Flexible Retrieval is for archives read about once a year, with retrieval in minutes to hours, a ninety-day minimum, and you must restore objects first. S three Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost archive, for data read less than once a year, with retrieval in hours, a one hundred eighty-day minimum, and a restore first. Retrieval fees apply to all three. One naming point: the older Amazon Glacier vault service no longer accepts new customers, and A W S recommends these S three Glacier classes instead. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, the minimum durations come from the S three user guide. Exam tip: cheapest long-term archive means Deep Archive; an archive with instant reads means Instant Retrieval.

1.title: S3 Lifecycle and Versioning
1.text: An S three Lifecycle configuration holds rules with two kinds of action. A transition action moves objects to another storage class, and an expiration action deletes them. In the figure, an object starts in Standard, moves to Standard-I A after thirty days, moves to Glacier Flexible Retrieval after a year, and then expires. Rules apply to existing and new objects, and they lower storage costs as data cools. S three Versioning is different. It keeps multiple versions of an object. An overwrite adds a version, and a delete adds a delete marker, so you can restore an earlier version after a mistake. Versioning is off by default. Once enabled it can only be suspended, and each version is billed. Exam tip: to move or delete data automatically as it ages, use a lifecycle policy.

1.title: Block Storage: Amazon EBS and Instance Store
1.text: Block storage comes in two forms for E C two. Amazon Elastic Block Store, or E B S, volumes are block storage attached to an instance and used like a hard drive. The data persists independently of the instance, and it is replicated within an Availability Zone. Use it for operating systems, databases and any data you keep, and you pay for what you provision. Instance store is temporary block storage on disks attached to the host. Its data is deleted when the instance stops, hibernates or terminates. Use it for buffers, caches and scratch data. There is no extra charge, because it is included in the instance price. E B S snapshots are point-in-time backups of volumes. S S D volumes suit transactional work, H D D volumes suit throughput, and encryption uses A W S K M S. Exam tip: a disk that survives the instance means E B S; temporary scratch space means instance store.

2.title: File Storage: Amazon EFS and Amazon FSx
2.text: For shared file storage there are two services. Amazon E F S is serverless, elastic file storage. It grows and shrinks automatically, speaks N F S, and can be shared by many E C two, E C S, E K S, Lambda and Fargate workloads at once. Choose a Regional file system, which spans multiple Availability Zones, or a One Zone file system. Think of it as shared Linux files. Amazon F S x is fully managed file systems in four kinds: Windows File Server, with S M B and Active Directory, and also NetApp On-tap, Open Z F S and Lustre. Think of it as Windows shares or specialist file systems. One caution: E F S is not supported on Windows-based E C two instances. Exam tip: a shared Linux file system means E F S, and Windows file shares mean F S x for Windows File Server.

2.title: AWS Storage Gateway: Cloud Storage for On-Premises Apps
2.text: A W S Storage Gateway connects an on-premises software appliance to cloud storage, so your existing applications can use A W S storage through standard protocols. You run it as a virtual machine or hardware appliance on site, or as an E C two instance. Look at the figure: applications talk to the gateway, which keeps a local cache and stores the data in A W S. An S three File Gateway gives N F S and S M B file shares that are stored as S three objects, with local caching for low latency. A Volume Gateway offers I S C S I volumes. Cached volumes keep data in S three and hot data locally, while stored volumes keep all data local, with snapshots in S three. A Tape Gateway replaces tape libraries. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, the documentation also lists an F S x File Gateway, so check for the current types. Exam tip: on-premises files or volumes backed by A W S storage, with a local cache, means Storage Gateway.

2.title: AWS Backup and AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
2.text: Two services protect your data and your servers. A W S Backup centralizes and automates backups across A W S services, such as E C two, E B S, S three, R D S, DynamoDB, E F S and F S x. You define backup plans, which are policies, and you can select resources by tag. Backups can move to a cold storage tier on a lifecycle, be copied across Regions and accounts, and be locked with Vault Lock, which enforces write-once-read-many. A W S Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates servers, on premises or in the cloud, to a low-cost staging area in A W S. When disaster strikes, it launches recovery instances within minutes. You can run drills and fail back later. Exam tip: scheduled, policy-based backups mean A W S Backup, and fast server recovery after a disaster means Elastic Disaster Recovery.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: Storage
2.text: Here is how the exam frames storage. Object, block or file: S three, E B S or instance store, E F S or F S x. Which S three class: frequent, unknown pattern, infrequent, re-creatable, or archive. Lifecycle or versioning: move and delete on a schedule, or keep and restore old versions. E B S or instance store: survives the instance, or temporary. E F S or F S x: shared Linux files, or Windows shares and specialist systems. Storage Gateway: on-premises access backed by A W S storage. And Backup or Elastic Disaster Recovery: policy-based copies, or fast server recovery. Exam tip: match the access pattern and durability need to the cheapest class that fits.

2.title: Design Check: Tidewater's Storage Plan
2.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Millions of product photos, served over the internet: Amazon S three, in Standard or Intelligent-Tiering. Order records kept for years and rarely read: S three Glacier Deep Archive, moved there by a lifecycle rule. Recover an accidentally overwritten file: S three Versioning. A fast disk for the database server: an Amazon E B S volume. Temporary scratch space for image processing: instance store. One set of files shared by the Linux web servers: Amazon E F S. Warehouse files kept on site, but backed by the cloud: A W S Storage Gateway. And consistent backups, plus fast recovery of servers: A W S Backup and Elastic Disaster Recovery. Pause the video if you want more time.

2.title: Try It: A Bucket, Versioning and a Lifecycle Rule (Optional)
2.text: This optional exercise is not tested on the exam, but it makes the storage ideas stick. Use a practice account. Create a bucket, remembering that the name must be unique, and upload a small text file. Turn on versioning, change the file, upload it again, and list the versions to see both. Then add a lifecycle rule that moves objects to Standard-I A after thirty days and expires them after three hundred sixty-five days. The two commands on the screen create a bucket and turn on versioning; the bucket name is only an example. When you finish, clean up: delete every version, then the bucket. Exam tip: hands-on work is not tested on this exam, but it makes the storage classes memorable.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. For types, object is S three, block is E B S and instance store, and file is E F S and F S x. For S three classes, Standard is for frequent use, Intelligent-Tiering for unknown patterns, the I A classes for infrequent use, and the Glacier classes for archives. Lifecycle rules transition and expire objects, and versioning lets you restore earlier copies. E B S is a disk that persists, and instance store is temporary scratch space. For hybrid and protection, Storage Gateway gives on-premises access, Backup applies policies, and Elastic Disaster Recovery gives fast recovery.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Tidewater's customers upload product photos that must be stored durably, at any scale, and served over the internet. Which service fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, Amazon S three, with the photos stored as objects in a bucket. S three stores any amount of data as objects, durably, and serves it to the internet. E B S and instance store give disks to individual servers, and E F S provides a shared file system rather than object storage.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Tidewater keeps order records for seven years, almost never reads them, and can wait hours to retrieve one. Which S three storage class has the lowest cost for this data? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, S three Glacier Deep Archive. It is the lowest-cost class for data read less than once a year, when hours of retrieval time are acceptable. The other classes cost more, because they keep millisecond access or add automatic tiering.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Log files are read often for thirty days, rarely after that, and can be deleted after a year. What should Tidewater configure to move and then delete them automatically? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, an S three Lifecycle configuration with transition and expiration actions. It moves objects to cheaper classes and expires them on a schedule. Versioning keeps old versions, replication copies objects between buckets, and Storage Gateway connects on-premises systems to A W S storage.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Tidewater's Linux web servers run on several E C two instances and must read and write the same set of files at the same time. The storage should grow and shrink automatically. Which service fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, Amazon E F S. It is serverless, elastic file storage that many instances can mount at once. An E B S volume serves one instance, instance store is temporary, and Glacier Deep Archive is an archive that cannot be mounted as a file system.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Select two. Which two statements about E C two instance store and Amazon E B S are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and D. Instance store is temporary, so its data is deleted when the instance stops or terminates, while an E B S volume keeps its data independently of the instance. Instance store is included in the instance price, E B S is the persistent option, and snapshots are stored separately as backups.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Tidewater wants one place to define backup schedules and retention for its E C two volumes, R D S databases and E F S file systems, and to copy backups to another Region. Which service should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, A W S Backup. It centralizes policy-based backups across services and can copy them across Regions. Storage Gateway connects on-premises systems, versioning keeps object versions in one bucket, and Elastic Disaster Recovery replicates servers for fast recovery.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all six answers. Question one: B. Question two: D. Question three: C. Question four: A. Question five: B and D. Question six: D. That completes Module eight. Next, Module nine covers the database services: relational, no S Q L, in-memory, and the tools to migrate to them.
